title: Morning Movers: Tiffany Tanks, Overstock Slumps, Adobe Gains - Barron's
text:
The Dow Jones Industrial Average is little changed this morning as quadruple witching is expected to dominate trading today . In today's Morning Movers , we...
•...look at today's housing-starts data;
•...highlight earnings in Tiffany and Adobe;
•...and consider the future of tech in The View From Silicon Valley.
Stocks Another day, another data disappointment. But the market doesn't seem to mind...at least not yet.
Illustration: Bloomberg News S&P 500 futures have advanced 0.1%, while Dow Jones Industrial Average futures have ticked up 9 points. Nasdaq Composite futures are little changed.
This morning, we learned that February housing starts came in at an annualized rate of 1.236 million, below forecasts for 1.29 million. Single family starts were a bit better--902,000 versus 877,000 expected--but still 10% below the 25-year average, writes Peter Boockvar, chief investment officer at Bleakley Advisory Group. "The most needed area of new homes are for those priced below $250k and it's gotten really difficult to supply that at a profitable margin," he explains. "The housing industry is in the new tug of war between a rise in incomes and jobs on one hand and rising mortgage rates, persistent home price gains at triple the rate of consumer price inflation and the limit on mortgage deductibility for higher end homes."
For more on housing, read Lawrence Strauss's recent cover story, The Housing Market's Rebound Is Far From Over . — Ben Levisohn
Morning Movers Adobe Systems (ADBE) is up 3.9% to $227.50 on its fiscal first-quarter earnings . The maker of design software said it earned $1.55 a share on revenue of $2.08 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of $1.44 a share on revenue of $2.05 billion. For the current quarter, it expects to earn $1.53 a share on revenue of $2.15 billion, compared to the consensus of $1.50 a share on $2.13 billion in sales.
Broadcom (AVGO) is down 0.7% to $265.90 after reporting fiscal-first quarter earnings . The chipmaker said it earned $5.12 a share on revenue of $5.33 billion. Analysts were looking for earnings of $5.05 a share on revenue of $5.32 billion. For the current quarter, it sees sales coming in at $5 billion, plus or minus $75 million, which is in line with consensus. Broadcom officially gave up its bid for Qualcomm (QCOM) earlier this week after the government blocked it , but there’s still plenty of M&A interest surrounding the stock.
CBS (CBS) is up 0.7% to $51.39 after Loop Capital initiated coverage with a Buy rating.
Illustration: Bloomberg News Dominion Energy (D) is down 1% to $70.55 after JPMorgan and UBS downgraded it to Neutral.
Hibbett Sports (HIBB) is down 2.2% to $22 on its fourth-quarter earnings . The athletic retailer earned 51 cents a share on revenue of $266.7 million, while analysts were expecting earnings of 44 cents on revenue of $261.37 million. For the full year, it expects to earn between $1.65 and $1.95 a share, below the $2.05 per-share consensus. Shares of fellow retailer Dick's Sporting Goods (DKS) took a tumble after reporting its fourth-quarter earnings .
Jabil (JBL) is up 4.6% to $29.80 after reporting fiscal second-quarter earnings . The Apple (AAPL) contractor said it earned 66 cents a share on revenue of $5.3 billion, while analysts had modeled for earnings of 62 cents a share on revenue of $4.9 billion. For the current quarter, it sees earnings of 35 cents to 55 cents on revenue of $4.75 billion to $5.05 billion. Analysts are looking for earnings of 45 cents a share on revenue of $4.82 billion.
Overstock.com (OSTK) is down 14.2% to $41.25 after the online retailer warned of potential ' material adverse effect ' from an investigation by the Securities and Exchange Commission into its tZero fintech subsidiary over recent ICO offering. It also reported fourth-quarter earnings .
Tiffany (TIF) is down 5.6% to $96.93 on its fourth-quarter earnings . The jeweler said it earned $1.67 a share on revenue of $1.33 billion, while analysts were looking for earnings of $1.63 a share on revenue of $1.32 billion. Comparable sales rose 3% in the quarter. For the full year, it expects to earn between $4.25 and $4.45 a share, compared to the $4.42 per-share consensus. "Recognizing the pressure points, we view the shares as attractive, given an expected ongoing improvement in sales (despite Jan’s deceleration), coupled with a story replete with self-help levers, which management appears to be closely examining," writes Instinet analyst Simeon Siegel.
Ulta Beauty (ULTA) is up 0.9% to $207.90 after reporting fourth-quarter earnings . The beauty products seller said it earned $2.75 a share, below the $2.78 per-share consensus, on revenue of $1.94 billion, which matched analysts’ expectations. For the current quarter, it sees earnings between $2.43 and $2.48 a share on revenue of $1.506 billion to $1.519 billion, while the Street is looking for earnings of $2.66 a share on revenue of $1.52 billion. Loop Capital's Anthony Chukumba reiterated a Buy rating and $300 price target on the stock: He admits that the quarter and guidance disappointed, but takes "some semblance of comfort in the fact we believe many investors expected management to guide to a lower F2018 operating margin."
Wendy's (WEN) is up 1.5% to $17.01 after Mizuho initiated coverage with a Buy rating.
Western Digital (WDC) is up 2% to $104.30 after Robert W. Baird upgraded it to Outperform. — Teresa Rivas
The View From Silicon Valley The Future Today Institute has glimpsed into the years ahead, and what it sees is lots of A.I., robots and space travel.
Illustration: iStockphoto The nonprofit organization’s 11th annual Tech Trends Report identified 235 advancements in emerging technologies — artificial intelligence, autonomous robots, space travel and green energy — as they enter the mainstream and reshape business, geopolitics and everyday life worldwide.
Here are the big trends they spotted:
1) 2018 marks the beginning of the end of traditional smartphones .
2) The field of artificial intelligence –– flush with capital and commercial applications, yet the subject of misplaced optimism and fear –– will continue to flourish.
3) Policymakers won’t be prepared to deal with new challenges that arise from emerging science and technology. Consequently, society is likely to see regulations, rules and legislation that are either too restrictive or don’t acknowledge that science and tech are in constant motion.
4) Consolidation of power among a small cadre of information and technology companies will continue.
“More important than the trends themselves is the relationship between them,” says Amy Webb, founder of the Future Today Institute and professor at the NYU Stern School of Business. “This year especially, the connective tissue between disparate trends — artificial intelligence, genetic editing, autonomous travel, collaborative robotics and cryptocurrencies — is especially strong.”
“For the first time in 11 years, we have devoted a significant portion of the report to China, which is quickly becoming a global leader in A.I.,” Webb adds. “The impact is reverberating across numerous industries and adjacent areas of technology development.” — Jon Swartz
